question: Let f(x) = 3 if x = −5; f(x) = −0.6 if −5 < x ≤ −2; f(x) = x² − 4 if −2 < x < 3; f(x) = x + 2 if x ≥ 3. Sketch the graph of f and evaluate lim_{x→−5} f(x), lim_{x→−2} f(x) and lim_{x→3} f(x).
Let f(x) = 4|x² − 1|/(x − 1) if x ≠ 1 and f(1) = 5. Find the largest interval(s) on which f is continuous, and show the function on a graph.
Determine the values of the constants a and b so that f is continuous, and show the continuous function on a graph: f(x) = x² + 1 if x < a; f(x) = 15 − 5x if a ≤ x ≤ b; f(x) = 5x − 25 if x > b.
Find the equation of the line tangent to the graph of y = x² − 5x + 1 at the point(s) where the curve crosses the line y = 7. Draw the curve, the line y = 7 and the tangent line(s).
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = 1/x + x² which has a slope of −3, and show the curve and the tangent line(s) on a graph.
Find the value of k so that the line y = −8x + k is tangent to the curve y = 3x² + 4x + 1. Also find the normal line at the point of contact, and draw the curve with both lines.
Find the equation of the line tangent to f(x) = √(9 − x²) at x = 2, and the normal line at that point. Draw the curve, the tangent and the normal.
Find the equation of the line tangent to f(x) = (ln x)/x at x = e and the normal line there. Draw the graph of f with both lines, showing its asymptotes, intercept, maximum and inflection point.
For f(x) = x⁴ − 8x² + 6 find the critical numbers, the local extreme values, the intervals of monotonicity, the intervals of concavity and the inflection points, then sketch the graph.
For f(x) = (x² − 2x + 4)/(x − 2) find the critical numbers, local extreme values, intervals of monotonicity, intervals of concavity and inflection points, and sketch the graph with its asymptotes.
Sketch the graph of f(x) = (x² + x − 20)/(x² + 4x − 5). Show its hole, its asymptotes and intercepts, and say where it is increasing and how it bends.
Find the local maximum and minimum values of f(x) = x/(1 + x)², and sketch its graph showing the asymptotes, intervals of increase and decrease, concavity and inflection point.
For f(x) = (x − 1)/(x² + 8), find the intervals where f is increasing or decreasing, its local extrema and inflection points, and draw the graph.
Find the intervals in which f(x) = x^(1/3)(x + 3)^(2/3) is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing, then sketch the graph, showing its cusp, vertical tangent, concavity and slant asymptote.
Find the local maximum and minimum values of f(x) = (x² − 4)^(2/3) and sketch the graph, including where it is concave up or down.
Identify the critical numbers and find the absolute maximum and minimum of f(x) = 3x⁵ − 20x³ on [−2, 2]. Then sketch the graph on that interval with its inflection points.
Find the intervals in which f(x) = (x² − 1)³ is increasing or decreasing, its local extreme values and its inflection points, and sketch the graph.
Find the intervals in which f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² + 5 is strictly increasing or decreasing, then sketch the graph showing every extreme point, the inflection point and the x-intercept.
Let f(x) = x²|9 − x²|/(3 − x). Is f continuous at x = 3? Sketch the graph of f, showing what happens at x = −3 and at x = 3, and its turning points.
Find the intervals in which f(x) = xeˣ − 4 is increasing or decreasing, and sketch its graph showing the minimum, the inflection point, the intercepts and the asymptote.
Find the intervals in which f(x) = |ln x| is increasing or decreasing and sketch its graph. Where is f not differentiable, and how does it bend?
Find the point on the graph of f(x) = x² that is closest to the point (2, 1), and show it on a graph.
Find the points on the graph of f(x) = x² + 1 that are closest to the point (0, 4). Show the curve, the point and the shortest distances on a graph.

Estimate the area of the region bounded by the graph of f(x) = x³ and the x-axis between x = 1 and x = 2 by dividing [1, 2] into (a) 5 subintervals (b) 10 subintervals (c) n subintervals of equal length. Use inscribed (left-endpoint) and circumscribed (right-endpoint) rectangles, and draw the rectangles for n = 5. What is the exact area?

The area under the curve y = 5 − 2x² + 4x³ − x⁵ from x = −1/2 to x = 3/2 is divided into n strips, each approximated by a rectangle of width 2/n. What is the limit of the sum of the areas of all the rectangles as n → ∞? Show the curve with some of the strips.
Find the area of the region enclosed between the curves y = x³/(x² + 1) and y = x/2. Draw the curves and shade the region.
Find the area of the region bounded by the curve y = x⁴ − x² and the line y = 3. Draw it and shade the region.
Find the area of the region enclosed by f(x) = 4 − x² and g(x) = 3x. Show the curves and shade the region.
Determine the area of the region enclosed by the graphs of x = −y² and x = 9 − 2y². Integrate with respect to y, and draw the region shaded.
Find the area of the region bounded by the graph of f(x) = |x² − 1|, the x-axis and the lines x = −3 and x = 2. Sketch and shade it.
Find the area of the region bounded by the graph of f(x) = x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6, the x-axis and the lines x = −2 and x = 3. Draw it and shade the region.

Find the volume of the solid of revolution about the x-axis generated by revolving the region enclosed by f(x) = sin x and g(x) = cos x from x = 0 to x = π/2. Show the region and the axis of rotation.
Find the volume of the solid generated by revolving about the x-axis the region enclosed by f(x) = x² and g(x) = |x| from x = −2 to x = 2. Draw the region and the axis.
Find the volume of the solid generated when the region bounded by y = 3x and y = x² + 2 rotates about the x-axis. Show the region and the axis of rotation.
Find ∫ (2x − 3) dx and sketch the family of antiderivatives for C = −1, 0 and 1.
Evaluate ∫₋₁² (x² − 1) dx and shade the region it measures, above and below the x-axis. The function is f(x) = x² − 1 on [−1, 2].
Find the average value of f(x) = x² on [0, 3] and show it on a graph.
A particle moves along a line with velocity v(t) = t² − 4t + 3 m/s for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Find its displacement and the total distance travelled, and show both on a velocity–time graph.
Find the area of the triangle-shaped region bounded by the lines y = x, y = 2x and y = 3 − x, and shade it.
The region between y = x² and y = x is revolved about the line y = −1. Find the volume using washers, and sketch the region, the axis of revolution and a typical washer.
The region bounded by y = x − x² and the x-axis is revolved about the y-axis. Find the volume by cylindrical shells and sketch the region with a typical shell.
The region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is revolved about the x-axis. Find the volume and sketch the region with a typical disc.
Approximate the area under f(x) = 4 − x² on [0, 2] with 4 rectangles using upper and lower sums, and draw the upper rectangles.
The region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is revolved about the x-axis. Find the volume and sketch the region with a typical disc.
Let f(x) = 2ˣ if x ≤ 1, and f(x) = 1 + 1/x if x > 1. Find the area of the region enclosed by the graph of f and the x-axis between x = −1 and x = 2, and show it on a graph.

Find, by integration, the area of the triangle-shaped region whose vertices are (−4, −1), (0, 0) and (5, 4). It is bounded by the lines y = x/4, y = 4x/5 and the line through (−4, −1) and (5, 4). Draw the three lines and shade the region.
Find the area of the region enclosed by f(x) = x, y = 1/x and y = 4. Draw the three graphs and shade the region.
Integrate 5/(2x) with respect to x, then sketch the members of the family of antiderivatives with c = −1, 0 and 1 on one graph.
Find the area of the region in the first quadrant which is enclosed by the y-axis and the curves f(x) = cos x and g(x) = sin x. Show it on a graph.
Evaluate ∫ from −π/2 to π/2 of sin x dx. What is this definite integral representing? Show it on a graph.
Find the volume of the solid of revolution generated when the region enclosed by the curve y = eˣ, the y-axis and the line y = e rotates about the y-axis. Sketch the region and the axis.

Check that f(x) = x² + 3x + 1, g(x) = x² + 3x, h(x) = x² + 3x − 12 and k(x) = x² + 3x + π all have the same derivative 2x + 3. Then draw the graphs of f, g, h and k together on the same axes. What does this tell you about ∫(2x + 3) dx?

A particle P moves along a straight line OX with acceleration 3.5t m/s². When t = 2 s, P is 10 m from O and has velocity 15 m/s. Find the velocity and the displacement when t = 5 s. Draw the velocity–time graph and show the distance covered between t = 2 and t = 5 as an area.

The monthly base salary of a shoe salesperson is Birr 900. She gets a commission of 2% on all sales over Birr 10,000 during the month, and if the monthly sales are Birr 15,000 or more she also receives a Birr 500 bonus. If x is the monthly sales in Birr and f(x) her income in Birr, express f(x) in terms of x, discuss the continuity of f on [0, 25000], and draw the graph.
